newsitem.title: MONACO: SOCCER SHOWCASE-PEN PICTURES OF PSG PLAYERS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-PEN PICTURES OF PSG PLAYERS.

text.p: Pen pictures of Paris St Germain players most likely to play in Sunday's French first division match against Monaco:

Bernard Lama, goalkeeper, age 33. France's first choice in goal, but, after knee surgery in October, has lost his fine early season form which saw him to go seven games unbeaten. Good positional sense.
Jimmy Algerino, right back, 25. Former Monaco player who has recently won a first team place with Daniel Kenedy injured and Benoit Cauet preferred in midfield.
Alain Roche, central defender, 29. France international who has won the French league title with three clubs, Bordeaux, Marseille and PSG. Sorely missed in recent games with injury.
Paul Le Guen, centre-back, 32. Another veteran defender widely considered past his best, a view reinforced in the recent European Super Cup thrashing by Juventus.

Didier Domi, left back, 18. Product of PSG youth scheme who has won a place in the team following the departure of Jose Cobos to Espanyol of Barcelona and injury to Portuguese utility defender Daniel Kenedy.
Daniel Kenedy, full-back or defensive midfielder, 22. Joined PSG from Benfica in off-season but has had a mixed season with injury problems and been unable to hold down a regular first team place.

Bruno N'Gotty, midfield ballwinner or central defender, 25. Big player with fine long range shot. Good at free kicks. Prefers to play at the back, where he has twice been capped by France, but is more likely to appear in midfield against Monaco.
Laurent Fournier, midfielder, 32. Former Marseille player who appeared in the 1991 European Cup final. Temperamental, sent off in Super Cup first leg against Juventus last week.
Benoit Cauet, defensive midfielder, 27. Vital for PSG as a ballwinner, can also play at full back. Won French league title with former clubs Marseille and Nantes.

Vincent Guerin, attacking midfielder, 31. Busy France international who on good days is the team's motor, but had a dismal game against Juventus last week, giving away two goals. Is working hard in training to recover his standing.

Rai, forward, 31. Former Brazil captain with delicate touch who links midfield with strikers. Respected senior player and one of three spokesmen, along with Lama and Le Guen, for players in times of crisis.

Leonardo, playmaker, 27. Midfield dynamo chiefly responsible for PSG's best performances this season and sorely missed when absent, as against Juventus when he came on as substitute despite lack of full fitness. Hopes to overcome cold quickly and be fit to play on Sunday.
Jerome Leroy, midfielder, 22. Rose to the senior squad from club's youth scheme to establish himself firmly this season as understudy for Guerin or Leonardo.

Patrice Loko, striker, 26. France international with fewer goals this season than might be expected from man leading the attack but works hard creating space for advancing midfielders, a ploy that brought dividends early in the campaign.

Cyrille Pouget, striker, 24. Former France forward signed from Swiss club Servette in December and a likely starter in view of indifferent form of other strikers. Scored first goal for PSG in 3-0 French Cup win at Besancon on Sunday.

Julio Cesar Dely Valdes, striker, 29. Much travelled Panama international who looked on his way out early in the season but regained the club's confidence with crucial goals in recovery from previous crisis in November. But has gone off the boil again.
